# Pinned Python dependencies for the catalog / verify workflows.
#
# Installed with `python3 -m pip install --user --require-hashes
# --only-binary=:all: -r` so a runner can only pull a prebuilt wheel whose
# sha256 hash matches one of the entries.
# Hashes sit on the same line as each requirement: that is the only format
# accepted by recent pip in --require-hashes mode.
#
# Only linux distributions are listed because every workflow that reads this file
# runs on ubuntu-24.04 / ubuntu-24.04-arm (see .github/workflows/*.yml). Add
# windows/macos wheel hashes if a non-linux runner is ever added.
# NOTE: --require-hashes needs the FULL transitive closure of jsonschema
# (attrs, jsonschema-specifications, referencing, rpds-py, typing-extensions).
#
# Every requirement carries its WHEEL hash first, then its sdist hash. The wheel
# hash is what matters: without it pip picks the only link whose hash is allowed
# -- the sdist -- and builds it, which downloads an unpinned, unhashed build
# backend (hatchling, setuptools-scm, ...) that then executes arbitrary code in
# a job holding `packages: write` and `id-token: write`. Every install site also
# passes `--only-binary=:all:` so an sdist fallback is impossible even if a
# wheel hash is ever dropped from this file.
#
# Renovate bumps only the `==` version here, never the hashes, so a bump PR
# fails `pip install` until the hashes are regenerated. The procedure is in
# docs/skills/ci-tooling/SKILL.md ("Regenerating .github/requirements hashes").
